content.body: Imagine you're at a party and want to know everyone's name except your own. How would you quickly find out? In this lesson, we'll learn how to calculate the product of all numbers in an array except the one at each position. This is a clever array problem that teaches us to use what we've already seen.
content.title: Welcome

content.body:
• Apply the 'remember what we have already seen' mental model to solve array problems
• Implement a solution using prefix and suffix products
• Explain why we store products as values in our calculation
• Build the final result array step by step
content.title: What you'll learn
Try it
content.prompt: For array [1, 2, 3], what's the product of all numbers except the first element?
content.successMessage: Correct! For position 0 (value 1), the product of other numbers is 2 × 3 = 6.

content.title: Try a bigger array
content.prompt: For array [2, 3, 4, 5], what's the product except the element at index 2 (value 4)?
content.successMessage: Well done! 2 × 3 × 5 = 30. You multiplied all numbers except the one at position 2.

content.title: One more
content.prompt: For array [1, 2, 3, 4], calculate products for ALL positions except self. What pattern do you notice?
content.successMessage: Great observation! Position 0: 2×3×4=24, Position 1: 1×3×4=12, Position 2: 1×2×4=8, Position 3: 1×2×3=6. Each product uses numbers from both sides of the current position.

content.body: What you just did was calculate each product separately by multiplying all other numbers. For position i, you looked at all elements before i and all elements after i. This approach would require re-scanning the array for each position.
content.title: What you did

content.body: When the array has 10,000 numbers, calculating each product from scratch would be extremely slow. We'd be doing the same multiplications over and over. We need a smarter method that remembers what we've already calculated. Can't figure it out? Click Show me on the next step.
content.title: Why it gets hard

content.body: The secret is to remember what we've already seen. Instead of recalculating everything for each position, we can store running products as we move through the array. Think of it like keeping a notebook where we write down the product of all numbers to the left of our current position, and another notebook for products to the right.
content.title: Key idea
content.visualMetaphor: A notebook where we write down what we've seen and check it in one step.

content.body: We'll use two passes through the array. First pass: calculate running products from left to right (prefix). Second pass: calculate running products from right to left (suffix), combining with what we stored from the first pass.
content.title: The approach
content.illustratedExample:
Walkthrough with [1, 2, 3, 4]:
Left pass: result = [1, 1×1=1, 1×2=2, 2×3=6] (products of left elements)
Right pass: suffix = 1, result[3] = 6×1=6, suffix = 1×4=4, result[2] = 2×4=8, suffix = 4×3=12, result[1] = 1×12=12, suffix = 12×2=24, result[0] = 1×24=24
Final: [24, 12, 8, 6]

content.body:
1. Create result array filled with 1s (neutral value for multiplication)
2. First pass (left to right): store running product of all elements to the left of current position
3. Second pass (right to left): multiply running product of all elements to the right with what's already in result
4. Return the final result array
content.title: Steps

steps.title: Initialize the result array
steps.instruction: Create a function productExceptSelf that takes nums array. Initialize a result array with the same length as nums, filled with 1s.
steps.hint: Use Array(n).fill(1) to create an array of length n with all values set to 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've created the result array that will store our final products.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Remember to make the array the same length as nums and fill it with 1s.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's start with creating an array. Use Array(nums.length).fill(1) to initialize it properly.

steps.title: Calculate left products
steps.instruction: Add a variable leftProduct initialized to 1. Loop through nums from left to right (use for loop). For each position i, set result[i] = leftProduct, then update leftProduct *= nums[i].
steps.hint: The leftProduct tracks the product of all elements to the left of current position.
steps.expectedOutcome: result stores products of left elements
steps.feedbackCorrect: Excellent! Now result[i] contains the product of all numbers to the left of position i.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start. Remember to update leftProduct after setting result[i], and multiply it by nums[i].
steps.feedbackWrong: Think about it: for each position, we want the product of everything to the left. Store that in result[i], then include current nums[i] in leftProduct for the next position.

steps.title: Calculate right products
steps.instruction: Add a variable rightProduct initialized to 1. Loop through nums from right to left (start at nums.length-1). For each position i, multiply result[i] by rightProduct, then update rightProduct *= nums[i].
steps.hint: We're combining the left products (already in result) with right products as we move backward.
steps.expectedOutcome: result combines left and right products
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! Now each result[i] is leftProduct × rightProduct, which gives us product of all except nums[i].
steps.feedbackPartial: Almost there. Remember to multiply result[i] by rightProduct first, then update rightProduct with nums[i].
steps.feedbackWrong: We need to go backward through the array. Start i at nums.length-1 and decrement. Multiply what's already in result[i] by rightProduct, then include nums[i] in rightProduct.

steps.title: Return the result
steps.instruction: After both loops, return the result array.
steps.hint: Simply add 'return result;' at the end of your function.
steps.expectedOutcome: function returns the final result array
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! Your function now correctly returns the product array.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're almost done. Just need to return the result array.
steps.feedbackWrong: Don't forget to return the result array at the end of your function.

steps.title: Test with example
steps.instruction: Test your function with nums = [1, 2, 3, 4]. What does it return?
steps.hint: Call your function and log the result, or trace through the logic manually.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Excellent! Your function correctly returns [24, 12, 8, 6] for input [1, 2, 3, 4].
steps.feedbackPartial: Check your calculations. Remember: left pass then right pass, combining products.

content.body: Congratulations! You've implemented an efficient solution to 'Product of Array Except Self'. Remember: we used the 'remember what we have already seen' approach by storing running products in two passes. This avoids O(n²) time complexity and gives us O(n) time with O(1) extra space (excluding the result array). The key insight was to separate the problem into left products and right products, then combine them.
content.title: Done
